# Agent notes

## Checks

- Run `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` and `bun run compile` before you push. CI fails when `dist/` does not match
  `src/`, so commit the rebuilt `dist/` with every source change.

## UI preview

- `bun run preview -- --out bar.png` renders the tab bar with sample tabs (active, busy, waiting, unread, error).
- `--options '{"padding":1}'` passes plugin options, `--hover "<row text>"` hovers a row, and `--width` and
  `--height` set the size in cells.
- When a change affects what the bar shows, render it on the base branch and on your branch and post both images
  as "Before" and "After".

## Demo recordings

- `bun run record -- --out demo.gif --step "hover Dark mode" --step "close Flaky checkout"` records the real
  OpenCode TUI with this checkout's plugin to a GIF. It needs `opencode`, `ttyd` and `ffmpeg` on `PATH` (or
  `OPENCODE_BIN` and `TTYD_BIN`) and Playwright's Chromium. Run it without steps to see the step list.
- `--options '{"confirmClose":true}'` passes plugin options and `--sidebar` crops the GIF to the tab bar.
  `--plugin <path>` records another checkout, such as a worktree of the base branch.
- `--sessions sessions.json` replaces the sample tabs with a JSON array of `{ "project", "title" }`. Busy and
  unread tabs need a model run, so show those states with `bun run preview`. Sessions are created in the
  listed order, so the last one has the most recent activity.
- `expect <text>` and `expect-not <text>` steps fail the recording when the screen does not match, so a GIF
  doubles as a test. Put them after every action, for example `close Two`, `expect Close tab`, `key Enter`,
  `expect-not Two`. `expect-above <a> -> <b>` checks an order, such as `expect-above docs -> api`. A failed
  step stops the steps but still writes the GIF, then exits with an error.
- A check in a before-and-after recording should pass on the PR branch and fail on the base branch. A check
  that passes on both, such as `expect New session`, proves nothing about the change.
- Every PR that changes `src/` in a way the user can see or touch must include a GIF of the changed behaviour,
  before and after. A reviewer records them when the author did not: read the diff, script the new behaviour
  with `expect` checks, record it on the PR branch and on the base branch, and post the steps with the GIFs.

## Pull requests

- PRs are squash-merged and the title becomes the changelog entry, so it must be a Conventional Commit such as
  `feat: confirm before closing a tab` or `fix: keep the tab order after a restart`.

## Releases

- tagpr keeps a `chore: release vX.Y.Z` PR open; merging it tags the release and publishes the GitHub release.
- Do not bump the version, create a tag, or merge the release PR until the user has confirmed the change works in
  their OpenCode. Commit fixes locally and wait for that confirmation.

# opencode-better-tabs A plugin for the [OpenCode](https://opencode.ai) TUI (v2) that redraws the vertical session tab bar on the left: tabs are grouped by git repository, every group and tab has a visible keyboard shortcut, and each group header shows how many sessions are working, waiting for you, or unread. > Supports OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer. V1 is not supported.

The demo shows tabs grouped by repository, opening a tab with two shortcuts (`alt+2`, `alt+2`), moving a group up with `alt+↑`, and searching all tabs with `/tabs`. It uses made-up repositories and sessions; see `docs/demo.tape` to record it again. ## Features - **Grouped by repository.** Worktrees belong to their repository's group. Sessions outside any git repository get one group per directory, marked `no git`. - **Two-step shortcuts.** `alt+1` selects the first group; the group labels disappear and the tabs of that group show their own keys. Press one (`alt+3`) to open that tab. The selection resets after 3 s, or press `esc` (`alt+x`, `alt+esc`) to cancel. - **Activity counters** on each group header: | Mark | Meaning | |---|---| | `⠋2` (blue, animated) | sessions working | | `!1` (yellow) | sessions waiting for you (question, permission) | | `•3` (accent, red on error) | sessions with unread output | When the header runs out of room, `•` disappears first and `!` last. - **Collapsible groups.** Click a header to collapse it; a collapsed group still shows its active tab. Selecting a collapsed group with `alt+N` opens it until you pick a tab. - **Reorder groups** by dragging a header with the mouse, or select a group with `alt+N` and press `alt+↑` / `alt+↓`. The order is saved and the built-in tab order follows it. - **Reorder tabs** inside an expanded group by dragging them with the mouse. - **Sort by recent activity** with the `sort` option: the group and the tab where you last sent a message move to the top. - **Close tabs** with the `✕` that appears on hover, or with a middle click. - **Hide the bar** with a command, and show it again. ## Requirements - OpenCode V2 2.2.5 or newer, with vertical tabs. - Windows, macOS or Linux. No other tools are needed: the plugin ships compiled JavaScript. ## Install Install a release from GitHub with the OpenCode CLI. Pin the tag: a pinned install is cached and OpenCode can tell when a newer release exists. ```sh opencode plugin add github:igorovh/opencode-better-tabs#v0.5.0 ``` This adds the plugin to the global `plugins` array in `~/.config/opencode/opencode.jsonc`. Restart the TUI and the new tab bar replaces the built-in one. You can also add the entry to the config yourself: ```jsonc { "$schema": "https://opencode.ai/config.json", "plugins": ["github:igorovh/opencode-better-tabs#v0.5.0"] } ``` To move to a newer release, change the tag. To remove the plugin: ```sh opencode plugin remove github:igorovh/opencode-better-tabs#v0.5.0 ``` ## Keys and commands | Shortcut | Slash command | Action | |---|---|---| | `alt+` then `alt+` | | Select a group, then a tab in it | | `alt+↑` / `alt+↓` (group selected) | | Move the selected group | | `esc`, `alt+x`, `alt+esc` (group selected) | | Cancel the selection | | `p` | `/tabs` | Search all tabs | | | `/close`, `/archive` | Close the current tab (the session is kept) | | `h` | `/tabs-hide` | Show or hide the tab bar | | | | Palette: group tabs now, toggle automatic grouping, collapse or expand all | The key order is `1`–`9`, then `c g h i j k l m n o p q r s t u v w x y z`. `a b d e f` are skipped because OpenCode uses `alt+a/b/d/e/f` to edit the prompt. Groups and the tabs inside a group use the same order. ## Options The tab bar runs in the TUI, and OpenCode passes plugin options to the TUI only from `~/.config/opencode/cli.json` (or `$OPENCODE_CONFIG_DIR/cli.json`). Options in `opencode.jsonc` reach only the server part, which does nothing. Add an entry to `cli.json` whose `package` is exactly the same string as in `opencode.jsonc`, tag included: ```jsonc { "plugins": [ { "package": "github:igorovh/opencode-better-tabs#v0.5.0", "options": { "modifier": "alt", "keys": "123456789cghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz" } } ] } ``` `opencode plugin add` does not write options, so add this entry yourself. - `modifier`: modifier for the shortcuts, such as `alt`, `ctrl` or `ctrl+shift`. The default is `alt` because many terminals send `ctrl+1` as a plain `1`. An invalid value shows a warning and falls back to `alt`. - `keys`: the key pool, in order. Only `a`–`z` and `0`–`9` are used. - `confirmClose`: ask before closing a tab with the `✕` or a middle click. Default `false`, so the tab closes at once. The `/close` and `/archive` commands never ask: they are explicit. - `padding`: blank lines above and below the label of every row (tab, group header and `+ New session`), from `0` to `3`. Default `0`, so rows stay one line tall. Set it to `1` to give the hover and active backgrounds some air: the row grows to `1 + padding × 2` lines. Terminal rows are one cell tall, so a gap is a whole blank line. - `sort`: `"manual"` (default) keeps the order you set by dragging. `"recent"` puts the group and the tab whose session last started working first, so a tab moves once when you send a message, not while it works. Tabs that never ran count from when they were created. Dragging and `alt+↑` / `alt+↓` are off in this mode. To change or turn off a command shortcut, set its command ID under `keybinds` in the same `cli.json`. Use `"none"` to turn it off: ```jsonc { "keybinds": { "better-tabs.picker": "ctrl+t", "better-tabs.hide": "none" } } ``` The IDs are `better-tabs.picker` and `better-tabs.hide`. ## How it works The plugin renders an overlay on top of OpenCode's own vertical tab bar and reads its data from the `ui.tabs` plugin API. It does not patch OpenCode, so the built-in bar is still underneath, and resizing it resizes the overlay. The plugin ships JSX that is already compiled, in `dist/`. OpenCode compiles Solid JSX only for plugins outside `node_modules`, and a GitHub install lives in its package cache ([anomalyco/opencode#39986](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39986)). `dist/` imports only the modules OpenCode shares with plugins (`@opencode/plugin`, `@opentui/core`, `@opentui/solid`, `solid-js`), so the plugin uses the host's own copies. - **Hiding** writes `tabs.mode` to `cli.json`. Only that value changes; comments and other settings stay. If `OPENCODE_CLI_CONFIG_CONTENT` sets `tabs`, that wins and the toggle has no effect. - The plugin makes no network requests and runs no commands. ## Development Requires [Bun](https://bun.sh). ```sh git clone https://github.com/igorovh/opencode-better-tabs.git cd opencode-better-tabs bun install bun run typecheck bun test ``` The sources are in `src/`, but OpenCode loads `dist/`. Run `bun run compile` after a change and commit `dist/` together with the sources; CI fails when they differ. To preview a UI change, render the tab bar with sample tabs to a PNG: ```sh bun run preview -- --out bar.png ``` Pass plugin options with `--options '{"padding":1}'` and hover a row with `--hover ""`. When a change affects what the bar shows, render it on the base branch and on your branch and post both images as "Before" and "After". To run your checkout instead of the published plugin, put its path in `plugins` and keep the compiler running. OpenCode reloads the plugin whenever `dist/` changes. ```jsonc { "plugins": ["/path/to/opencode-better-tabs"] } ``` ```sh bun run compile --watch ``` ## License [MIT](LICENSE)
